learningObjectives: Extend the provided purchase ExecutionList with invoice verification, Excel output, file movement and email delivery.
Scan invoice text and verify the company, current order number and exercise total.
Create and save an Excel workbook using named worksheet/range references.
Distinguish the original course mail example from current provider authentication requirements.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What the Grand Scenario is for

elements.term: From isolated lessons to one business process
elements.description: The original AE1 Grand Scenario extends a Demo Web Shop fiction-book order into PDF verification, Excel output, file operations and email delivery. The initial base ExecutionList can generate the invoice and log out. In the supplied solution, the complete seven-entry ExecutionList runs login, ordering, PDF checks, Excel output, file movement, mail and finally logout. The course was developed with Tosca 16.0.

elements.text: The original downloadable package contains both base and solution subsets. Their Grand Scenario folder contains Precondition, Library, Process and Post condition. If an imported subset is not immediately visible, the Academy notes suggest searching under Section. Importing or reading a subset does not execute its tests.

bulletPoints: The capstone: one business flow, several engines, structured properly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Four extensions to the purchase flow

elements.description: Add invoice verification, Excel output, invoice movement and email delivery to the existing purchase ExecutionList. Within the Excel TestCase, the source uses Precondition, Process and Postcondition folders for opening/preparing, writing and saving/closing the workbook. These are training organization choices, not mandatory names for every Tosca test.

elements.title: The four new TestCases
items: Verify order invoice pdf — scan the downloaded invoice and check its values.
Copy data to Excel — create a workbook/worksheet/range, write headings and order data, save and close.
Move the pdf file — move/rename the downloaded invoice to the agreed destination.
Send the files in email — attach both the invoice and workbook, then run the four added TestCases through the purchase ExecutionList.

elements.text: Arrange cleanup on relevant failure paths. Sequential TestCases do not themselves guarantee that workbook closure or session cleanup executes after an earlier failure. Cleanup does not undo the order. Validate output files before dependent steps use them.

elements.title: Original solution ExecutionList order
items: Login to web shop
Order fiction book and pay on delivery
Verify order invoice pdf
Copy data to Excel
Move the pdf file
Send the files in email
Logout from the web shop

bulletPoints: Purchase ExecutionList → PDF assertions → Excel output → file movement → email with two attachments.

elements.term: The 'Login to web shop' reusable block
elements.description: Both supplied subsets contain a TestStepLibrary named Library and its Reusable TestStepBlock Login to web shop. The block contains Open demo web shop, Click on log in link and Provide log in details. The Login to web shop TestCase references this block and then separately verifies successful login.

References to a Reusable TestStepBlock share centrally maintained steps; changes affect all linked references. A resolved reference becomes an independent copy, so it no longer receives those changes. Updating shared steps still requires validating callers and their assertions.

elements.text: The supplied login TestCase keeps its success assertion outside the shared block. Other designs may share assertions when appropriate. The observed source structure is a course implementation choice, not a mandatory three-step rule for all reusable blocks.

bulletPoints: The supplied library shares three login actions; the caller separately verifies successful login.
Keep links and independent copies distinct when updating shared steps.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Copy the order data to Excel

elements.term: Workbook, worksheet and range are separate references
elements.description: The exercise creates Order_Details at C:\Tosca_Projects\Order_Details.xlsx using TBox Open Excel Workbook with Create New=True. It creates the Order_Details worksheet, then defines OrderDataRange from A1 to D5. The path and range are training values, not universal defaults.

elements.title: Prepare, write, then save
items: Precondition: open/create the named workbook, create its worksheet and define the named range.
Process: use TBox Excel Range Manipulation to select Data Table and $header. Input Company, OrderNumber and OrderTotal in $1, $2 and $3 respectively.
Process: select the first data row ($1), then Input Demowebshop, {B[orderNumber]} and 41.00 under the matching headings.
Postcondition: use TBox Close Excel Workbook with Workbook Name=Order_Details, Path=C:\Tosca_Projects and Save=True. Confirm the expected workbook exists before attaching it.

elements.text: The source writes specified company/total values and the buffered order number; it does not demonstrate an automatic generic PDF-to-Excel converter. 41.00 is the exercise expectation, not a fixed total for every shop order.

bulletPoints: Keep Workbook Name, Worksheet Name and Range Name distinct.
Select $header for headings and the data row for values; persist the workbook before the next step.

elements.term: Scan and verify the order fields
elements.description: After running the purchase ExecutionList, open its order_orderNumber.pdf output. Under the course’s Grand Scenario Modules folder, create PDF Modules and use PDF Scan to scan Order number, Company from Billing Information and Order total as Text. Save the Module as Order Invoice. In the invoice-verification TestCase, Input the Target PDF path and Verify Company=Demowebshop, Order number={B[orderNumber]} and Order total=41.00.

Downloading the invoice is not automatic PDF verification. The original exercise uses scanned text assertions; it does not prescribe a reference-file comparison or exclusion area. As an independent extension, use appropriate PDF Modules for selected comparison checks and verify the dynamic identifier separately rather than excluding an important mismatch.

elements.text: Tosca supports appropriate engine Modules within a business flow, subject to their prerequisites and compatibility. Reuse and buffering do not guarantee that every engine combination or document check works without configuration.

The supplied order TestCase verifies the confirmation line with Order number: {XB[orderNumber]}. This captures the dynamic identifier while verifying the message; subsequent invoice and Excel steps read {B[orderNumber]}. Keep the same buffer name throughout the flow rather than copying an identifier from a previous run.

bulletPoints: Target PDF uses Input; the three invoice fields use Verify.
The exercise total is 41.00; account for your actual test data rather than treating that amount as a universal product rule.

elements.description: The original exercise adds TBox Move/Rename File. Existing Path points to the actual downloaded invoice; New Path is C:\Tosca_Projects\Invoice.pdf. Both use Input. Later attachment steps must use this new path, not the original download name.

elements.text: Prepare the destination and check the operation’s result. Moving a file is not invoice-content verification and does not save the Excel workbook.

bulletPoints: Move/rename after validating the invoice, before sending the attachment.

elements.description: The source uses Connect to Exchange Server and Send Mail with the same MailConnection name, then attaches C:\Tosca_Projects\Invoice.pdf and C:\Tosca_Projects\Order_Details.xlsx. It directs the test message to the tester’s own address and adds the four new TestCases to the purchase ExecutionList.

elements.text: The Tosca 16.0 PDF contains a historical Direct-authentication EWS example with a username/password. Do not assume it works with today’s Microsoft accounts: Exchange Online removed Basic authentication for EWS, and current Outlook.com settings require OAuth2. Confirm supported Tosca/provider authentication and EWS availability before running the mail step; switching to a personal mailbox is not a general fix for an unsupported authentication method.

The source’s final IMAP hint incorrectly describes sending and uses an SMTP hostname. SMTP sends mail; IMAP accesses incoming mail. Current Outlook.com documentation lists smtp-mail.outlook.com:587 with STARTTLS for SMTP, and outlook.office365.com:993 with SSL/TLS for IMAP, with OAuth2. These Outlook.com settings must not be applied indiscriminately to Exchange Online tenants or other providers.

bulletPoints: The mail step needs both output files at their final paths.
A successful file move or workbook write does not prove an email was sent; check the mail operation/result independently.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Original purchase flow and Module inventory

elements.term: Three purchase phases in both subsets
elements.description: The supplied ordering TestCase has fourteen TestSteps: four navigation steps, seven checkout steps and three order-verification/download steps. The final solution includes four additional output TestCases before logout. These names and grouping are observed training data, not universal Tosca defaults.

elements.title: Supplied web and PDF Modules
items: Navigation elements: Top menu and Logged in screen.
Login: Login page.
Products: Product choice tabs, Add to cart and Books product selection_Old.
Checkout: Shopping cart, Billing address, Shipping address, Shipping method, Payment method, Payment information – COD and Check, Confirm payment, Order confirmation page and Download PDF Invoice.
Solution-only PDF Modules: Order Invoice.

elements.text: Static subset inspection confirms the objects and links, not successful execution against the current shop. Stored source execution logs are not a fresh test run. Revalidate current application controls and test data in a supported installed environment.

bulletPoints: The solution orders all seven TestCases and keeps logout last.
Original subset structure and buffer capture are now inspected; current shop execution remains a separate validation.

examPitfalls.title: Stopping at the shopping flow
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Finishing after the invoice download and logout.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The original capstone adds four TestCases for PDF verification, Excel output, file movement and mail delivery. The provided shopping flow is the starting point.

examPitfalls.title: Hard-coding the order number
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reading an order number from a manual run and typing it into the 'navigate to order details' step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Capture the current generated identifier and reference that value later. Buffering avoids assuming a known prior identifier; it does not establish that IDs differ on every execution.

examPitfalls.title: Using the old download path as an attachment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Moving the invoice but still attaching its original filename, or attaching an unsaved workbook.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the moved Invoice.pdf path and the saved Order_Details.xlsx output. Validate both files before sending.

examPitfalls.title: Duplicating the login steps instead of reusing the library block
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Copying the three login TestSteps into each TestCase that needs a logged-in session.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: References to a Reusable TestStepBlock share centrally maintained steps; changes affect all linked references. A resolved reference becomes an independent copy, so it no longer receives those changes. Updating shared steps still requires validating callers and their assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Treating the PDF invoice as out of scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ending the verification at the order confirmation page because the invoice is 'just a document'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Downloading the invoice is a browser/file operation, not automatic PDF verification. Verify the file is available, then use PDF Modules for the chosen checks. Content extraction and reference comparison are distinct operations. Configure explicit page/area exclusions only for allowed differences; verify the captured order identifier separately rather than hiding an important mismatch.

examPitfalls.title: Copying historical mail settings unchanged
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Direct/password-based EWS works for every Microsoft account or using IMAP as a sending protocol.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check current provider/product support and authentication. SMTP sends; IMAP receives/accesses mail. The source’s outdated or incorrect hints are not current configuration instructions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which four tasks does the original AE1 capstone add after its provided purchase flow?

options.text: Only login, order and logout.
Invoice verification, Excel output, invoice movement and email delivery.
One new TestCase for each browser page, without file or mail operations.
Smoke, Regression, One-time and Performance suites.

practiceQuiz.hint: Follow the invoice from download through delivery.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source extends the provided purchase ExecutionList with four TestCases: verify the invoice, write the order data to Excel, move the PDF and email both outputs.

optionExplanations.A: The shopping flow is the starting point, not the complete capstone.
optionExplanations.B: These are the four additional TestCases specified in the original exercise.
optionExplanations.C: The exercise combines document, spreadsheet, file and mail operations rather than only browser pages.
optionExplanations.D: These suite categories are not the original four extensions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why does the invoice-verification step use {B[orderNumber]} rather than an order number copied from a previous run?

options.text: To make the TestCase run faster.
Because later steps need the actual runtime identifier, rather than a value copied from a prior run.
Because buffers are required in every Tosca TestCase.
To satisfy the PDF Engine's anchor requirements.

practiceQuiz.hint: The value does not exist until the application creates it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Buffering captures the current order identifier for later use. The application decides its allocation behavior; the test should not assume every execution produces a different identifier.

optionExplanations.A: Buffering supplies the actual runtime value; it does not inherently promise faster execution.
optionExplanations.B: Capture the current identifier and consume it later rather than using a value from a previous run.
optionExplanations.C: Buffers are useful when a later step needs captured values, not mandatory in every TestCase.
optionExplanations.D: Capturing an order identifier is distinct from configuring PDF anchor identification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the supplied AE1 subsets, where are the shared login actions stored for linked reuse?

options.text: Duplicated in each TestCase that needs them, for independence.
In a TestStepLibrary as a Reusable TestStepBlock, so linked callers share centrally maintained steps.
In the Post condition, so they run last.
In a Module, since Modules are the reuse mechanism for TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.hint: The login TestCase references the shared three-action block, then verifies success.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The example uses a Reusable TestStepBlock in a TestStepLibrary. Changes affect linked references; resolved copies are independent and require their own updates.

optionExplanations.A: Independent copies require separate maintenance and do not provide linked reuse.
optionExplanations.B: A TestStepLibrary’s Reusable TestStepBlock centrally maintains linked references. Resolved copies are no longer linked.
optionExplanations.C: Login establishes the starting session in this example; it is not the logout cleanup action.
optionExplanations.D: Modules describe automation interfaces; the TestStepLibrary reuses sequences of TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which approach verifies a downloaded invoice rather than merely proving that a download completed?

options.text: The Excel Engine, using TBox Excel 1:1 File Compare.
Use scanned PDF text Modules to check the company, current order number and expected total.
The Mail Engine, since invoices are emailed.
No engine change is needed; XBrowser handles the PDF.

practiceQuiz.hint: Download completion and invoice correctness are different assertions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The original exercise scans three text fields and uses Verify for the company, buffered order number and expected total. Input identifies the Target PDF. A completed download alone establishes none of those content assertions.

optionExplanations.A: Excel file comparison is not PDF invoice verification.
optionExplanations.B: The scanned fields are explicitly checked against the expected company, runtime identifier and total.
optionExplanations.C: A downloaded PDF need not arrive through email; Mail Modules are not a PDF-content verifier.
optionExplanations.D: A browser download alone does not establish document content correctness.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which files does the original capstone attach to its mail message?

options.text: The moved Invoice.pdf and saved Order_Details.xlsx.
Only the original downloaded PDF; no workbook is created.
The custom-control DLLs from Lesson 06.
Only a screenshot of the order confirmation.

practiceQuiz.hint: The source combines the document output and spreadsheet output.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The mail step uses the moved invoice and saved workbook paths as two attachments. Both outputs must exist; this does not by itself verify delivery.

optionExplanations.A: These are the two output files named in the source mail step.
optionExplanations.B: The exercise creates and attaches the workbook as well as the moved PDF.
optionExplanations.C: Custom-control DLLs belong to a different lesson, not the capstone mail outputs.
optionExplanations.D: An order screenshot is not the prescribed invoice/workbook pair.

quickRecap.value: Run the provided purchase flow, then add PDF verification, Excel output, file movement and mail delivery.
Input Target PDF; Verify Demowebshop, {B[orderNumber]} and the exercise total 41.00.
Workbook/worksheet Order_Details; range OrderDataRange=A1:D5; $header for headings, $1 for the first data row.
Save/close Order_Details.xlsx; move the invoice to Invoice.pdf; attach both final files.
The historical Direct EWS example is not current Microsoft-account setup guidance. Check compatible modern authentication and provider support.
SMTP sends mail; IMAP accesses incoming mail. Do not copy the source’s incorrect IMAP-sending hint.
Library contains the linked Login to web shop block with three actions; the caller separately verifies success. Resolved copies no longer share updates.
Login → order → PDF checks → Excel output → move invoice → send attachments → logout.
